episode.title: Make callback delivery lazy-safe and force reload lifecycle-symmetric
episode.before: At parent eac1e25127a75c61116a0bbb8ce7681a2f8b61b4, module-level hook and middleware invocation and presence checks directly queried the process plugin manager without ensuring discovery. Processes that did not import the component whose side effect triggered discovery could therefore report no callback or silently skip delivery. Separately, full unload cleared manager-local hooks without restoring configuration-owned shell hooks, and it removed legacy platform registrations but did not deregister tool names tracked outside the ownership ledger, allowing missing configuration hooks and stale global tools after force reload.
episode.after: At 8be9c76f8c01f652e1c7acd576c37e4bdaed30be, callback delivery entry points obtain a delivery manager that joins in-flight background discovery and performs discovery when necessary while preserving compatibility with manager test doubles. Full unload also deregisters tracked tool names not represented by tool ownership records. After a successful forced discovery sweep, configuration-owned shell hooks are rebuilt from current configuration; restoration failures are logged and do not invalidate the completed reload.
episode.diff: The change adds a lazy-discovery delivery helper and routes module-level invoke_hook, invoke_middleware, has_hook, and has_middleware through it; adds a legacy-tool cleanup sweep during unload-all while excluding ownership-ledger tools; adds configuration-hook re-registration that resets registration idempotence and reloads configuration; invokes that reconciliation only after successful force rediscovery; and adds focused tests for lazy delivery, gate behavior, mock-manager compatibility, shell-hook restoration, fail-open restoration, and stale-tool cleanup. The commit modifies agent/shell_hooks.py, hermes_cli/plugins.py, and tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py with 282 insertions and 5 deletions.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 8be9c76f8c01f652e1c7acd576c37e4bdaed30be has parent eac1e25127a75c61116a0bbb8ce7681a2f8b61b4 and is titled "fix(plugins): hook delivery parity + symmetric force-reload (#64178)".
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller 8be9c76f8c01f652e1c7acd576c37e4bdaed30be; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: The pinned change modifies three implementation/test files with 282 insertions and 5 deletions.

In the parent, module-level invoke_hook and invoke_middleware directly used get_plugin_manager(), has_hook directly queried that manager, and has_middleware inspected the undiscovered manager without initiating discovery.
evidence_units.source: git diff eac1e25127a75c61116a0bbb8ce7681a2f8b61b4 8be9c76f8c01f652e1c7acd576c37e4bdaed30be -- hermes_cli/plugins.py; parent hermes_cli/plugins.py around former lines 5234-5268

evidence_units.claim: _delivery_manager obtains the active manager, treats managers without _discovered as already usable, joins background discovery when the real manager is undiscovered, invokes discover_and_load, and returns the resulting manager.
Module-level hook and middleware invocation and presence-gate functions now ensure discovery through _delivery_manager before dispatching or deciding that callbacks are absent.
A lifecycle producer checks has_hook before calling invoke_hook, demonstrating that an incorrect pre-discovery false result can suppress callback delivery entirely.

Delivery-parity tests construct an undiscovered manager and verify that module-level hook invocation, middleware invocation, and both presence gates trigger discovery and observe registered callbacks; another test verifies compatibility with a stub manager lacking _discovered.

The parent unload-all path swept legacy platform names and cleared manager-local tool tracking, but contained no corresponding global deregistration sweep for tool names lacking ownership-ledger registrations.
evidence_units.source: git diff eac1e25127a75c61116a0bbb8ce7681a2f8b61b4 8be9c76f8c01f652e1c7acd576c37e4bdaed30be -- hermes_cli/plugins.py; parent hermes_cli/plugins.py around former lines 3289-3324

evidence_units.claim: During unload-all, the implementation derives tool names covered by ownership records, selects tracked names outside that set, and best-effort deregisters only those legacy names from the process-global tool registry before clearing manager state.

A force-reload test places a tool name in manager tracking without an ownership record, calls unload, and asserts that the global deregistration operation received that name and that local tracking and discovery state were reset.
Force discovery already called unload, whose unload-all branch clears the manager's hook dictionary, but the parent had no post-discovery operation to reconstruct configuration-owned shell hooks.
evidence_units.source: git diff eac1e25127a75c61116a0bbb8ce7681a2f8b61b4 8be9c76f8c01f652e1c7acd576c37e4bdaed30be -- hermes_cli/plugins.py agent/shell_hooks.py; parent hermes_cli/plugins.py around former lines 3309-3424

evidence_units.claim: re_register_config_hooks clears the shell-hook idempotence set under its lock, loads current configuration, and passes it through the existing registration routine.

After a successful forced discovery sweep, discover_and_load invokes shell-hook reconciliation. The adapter catches ordinary restoration errors and logs them so an otherwise successful force reload remains discovered.

Force-reload tests verify that shell-hook reconciliation is not called for initial discovery, is called once for force discovery, and that a reconciliation exception does not prevent the manager from reaching discovered state.
The shell-hook helper test verifies that re-registration clears the prior idempotence key and supplies freshly loaded configuration to the existing registration routine.

The supplied evidence bundle classifies the pinned artifact as a training candidate with a resolved local implementation commit and implementation-plus-test changes, while explicitly noting that GitHub discussion metadata is unavailable.

candidate_atomics.name: ensure-discovery-before-callback-delivery
candidate_atomics.title: Discover extensions before checking or delivering callbacks
candidate_atomics.description: At callback-facing entry points, wait for any ongoing discovery and lazily discover extensions before invoking hooks or middleware or using their presence as a delivery gate.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent extension callbacks from being silently absent in processes whose startup path did not explicitly trigger extension discovery.
semantic_action.pre_state: A callback invocation or presence check reaches an extension manager whose discovery sweep may not have run or may still be running.
semantic_action.post_state: The real manager has completed discovery before callback lookup or dispatch, while injected manager substitutes without lifecycle state continue to be called unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Construct an undiscovered manager whose discovery sweep installs hook and middleware callbacks; assert invocation and presence checks make it discovered and observe the callbacks, then assert a lifecycle-less stub manager remains usable.

candidate_atomics.name: remove-unowned-legacy-registrations-on-full-unload
candidate_atomics.title: Remove legacy global registrations during full unload
candidate_atomics.description: Reconcile manager-local legacy registration tracking with the global registry while preserving entries whose teardown and restoration are controlled by ownership records.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent stale extension-provided capabilities from surviving a full unload or force reload in a long-lived process.
semantic_action.pre_state: A full unload is processing tracked global registration names, some of which may predate or bypass the current ownership ledger.
semantic_action.post_state: Tracked names without corresponding ownership records are best-effort removed from the global registry, ledger-controlled names are left to precise handle disposal, and local lifecycle state is cleared.
semantic_action.validation: Seed manager-local tracking with a name that has no ownership record, invoke full unload, and assert exactly that name is deregistered and local tracking and discovery state are reset.

candidate_atomics.name: restore-configuration-owned-hooks-after-force-reload
candidate_atomics.title: Restore configuration-owned hooks after force reload
candidate_atomics.description: After forced extension rediscovery succeeds, rebuild hooks owned by external configuration that were cleared by the extension manager's full unload but cannot be restored by extension ownership records.

semantic_action.intent: Preserve configured callback behavior across a force reload without making ancillary restoration failure invalidate the successful extension sweep.
semantic_action.pre_state: A force reload has cleared the manager's callback state and completed extension rediscovery, while configuration-owned hook registrations and their idempotence markers may describe the pre-unload state.
semantic_action.post_state: Registration idempotence state is reset and hooks are rebuilt from current configuration; if rebuilding raises an ordinary exception, the extension manager remains successfully discovered.
semantic_action.validation: Assert normal discovery does not invoke reconciliation, forced discovery invokes it once, a reconciliation exception does not unset discovered state, and the helper clears prior idempotence state before registering freshly loaded configuration.

candidate_workflows.name: make-callback-delivery-independent-of-startup-surface
candidate_workflows.title: Make extension callback delivery independent of startup path
candidate_workflows.description: Establish a callback-delivery boundary that lazily completes extension discovery before both presence gating and dispatch, including processes that omitted the usual discovery-triggering import.

workflow_graph.goal: Every supported process surface can observe and deliver installed extension callbacks even when its startup path did not explicitly initialize extensions.
when_to_use: Some process surfaces invoke shared callback APIs without a guaranteed earlier extension-discovery call.
Callers use a callback-presence predicate as a gate before dispatch, so a pre-discovery false result can suppress delivery.
anti_goals: Do not require every caller or startup surface to duplicate extension initialization.
Do not force discovery for injected test doubles or adapters that intentionally lack the real manager's lifecycle state.
Do not change callback return aggregation or callback argument semantics.
not_applicable_when: The callback registry is statically constructed before any caller can access it.
The API is intentionally defined to expose only already-loaded extensions and must never initiate loading.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A callback invocation or gate is about to run, but the active real manager may be undiscovered or have discovery in flight.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Discovery is complete before callback lookup and dispatch, and installed callbacks are observable through both presence gates and invocation APIs.

steps.condition: Apply when the active manager exposes lifecycle state indicating discovery has not completed; otherwise dispatch directly.
steps.validation: From an undiscovered manager, verify hook invocation, middleware invocation, and both presence gates complete discovery and observe callbacks; verify a manager substitute without lifecycle state is invoked unchanged.

validation_ladder: Unit-check that the delivery helper joins ongoing discovery and invokes discovery only for an undiscovered real manager.
Verify direct hook and middleware invocation returns values from callbacks registered during lazy discovery.
Verify presence gates return true after lazy discovery so gate-before-invoke call sites do not suppress delivery.
Verify compatibility with manager substitutes that do not expose internal lifecycle fields.
stop_conditions: Stop if there is no stable central boundary shared by callback gates and dispatch operations.
Stop if initiating discovery from callback delivery would violate the API's documented side-effect contract.
Stop if discovery cannot be synchronized safely with an existing background sweep.
unresolved_or_deferred: The changed tests model non-initializing surfaces through an undiscovered manager; no end-to-end test for each named dashboard, TUI, query, cron, or gateway surface was added in this commit.

candidate_workflows.name: make-force-reload-reconcile-cross-owner-state
candidate_workflows.title: Make force reload reconcile legacy and configuration-owned state
candidate_workflows.description: During a full extension reload, remove stale global registrations not covered by the current ownership mechanism, then restore non-extension callback state that the unload necessarily cleared.

workflow_graph.goal: A forced extension reload leaves neither stale extension-owned global capabilities nor missing configuration-owned callbacks.
when_to_use: A force reload performs full teardown before rediscovery in a long-lived process.
Some tracked registrations can predate the current ownership ledger or bypass it.
The extension manager's local callback container also contains callbacks owned by external configuration.
anti_goals: Do not blanket-remove ledger-controlled registrations after their handles have restored displaced entries.
Do not treat configuration-owned callbacks as extension-owned ledger entries.
Do not run post-reload restoration during ordinary first discovery.
Do not abort an otherwise successful extension reload solely because ancillary configuration-hook restoration fails.
not_applicable_when: All global registrations are provably represented by authoritative ownership records and full unload cannot contain legacy state.
Full unload does not clear any state owned by another configuration or subsystem.
Reload is implemented by process replacement, so no in-process registry state survives.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A long-lived manager is beginning forced rediscovery and may contain both ledger-owned registrations, legacy tracked global registrations, and configuration-owned callbacks in manager-local collections.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Legacy unowned global registrations are absent, ledger restoration is preserved, extensions have been rediscovered, and configuration-owned callbacks have been rebuilt from current configuration or restoration failure has been contained without falsifying discovery success.

steps.condition: Run only for full unload; select tracked global names that have no matching ownership record.
steps.validation: Assert an unowned tracked name is deregistered and lifecycle-local tracking is cleared; ensure ledger-owned names are excluded by construction.

steps.condition: Run only after the forced discovery sweep and its normal post-discovery refresh complete successfully.
steps.validation: Assert forced discovery invokes restoration exactly once, normal initial discovery does not, current configuration is passed to registration after idempotence reset, and restoration failure leaves discovery successful.

validation_ladder: Unit-test classification of tracked registrations into ownership-controlled and legacy-unowned sets.
Verify legacy-unowned global entries are removed during full unload while manager-local state returns to undiscovered and empty.
Verify configuration-hook idempotence state is cleared and current configuration is reprocessed.
Verify hook restoration occurs only after a forced successful sweep.
Inject restoration failure and verify the completed reload remains marked discovered.
stop_conditions: Stop if registration ownership cannot be distinguished reliably; blanket deregistration could delete a restored prior entry.
Stop if the supposedly external callback state is actually owned and restored by the extension ownership mechanism.
Do not run restoration after a failed discovery sweep.
Escalate if restoration is safety-critical and fail-open behavior is not acceptable for the host application.
unresolved_or_deferred: The implementation deliberately handles registry import and individual legacy deregistration failures as debug-logged best-effort cleanup; the added tests do not exercise those failure branches.
No integrated test proves the complete unload-discover-config-rebuild sequence with a real configuration file and real global registry.

Targeted tests were inspected but could not be executed in the provided checkout environment: the initial pytest command was unavailable, and an isolated pinned worktree attempt did not materialize the requested test path.

unresolved_questions: GitHub issue body, comments, reviews, timeline, and status checks were unavailable in the supplied bundle, so rationale is limited to the commit message, implementation, call sites, and tests.

Why the supplied repository's current checkout is at 9a6108fdf29bb789520fd5b10f9cb01a2cbf311d rather than the pinned ref is not established; all semantic claims above use git objects from the pinned commit and its parent.
